themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions complaints exploded to 37 THIS WEEK versus a 4.8-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks—a 679% spike (z-score: 12.96)—suggesting a sudden, widespread deterioration of pavement, potholes, or street infrastructure across Morningside Heights/Hamilton Heights that demands immediate field verification.
evidence: 37 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (679% increase)
Z-score of 12.96 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Community Board has repeatedly requested sanitation truck funding, suggesting chronic infrastructure issues
reporting_angles: Field canvassing: photograph worst-affected blocks; identify whether single event (water main break, construction damage) or district-wide pattern
Department of Sanitation response: why the sudden spike, what's the repair timeline, is snow/weather a factor

themes_detail.label: Electrical System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints nearly doubled to 34 LAST WEEK compared to a 15.2-per-week average over the prior 8 weeks—a 123% spike—raising concerns about aging electrical infrastructure, potential fire hazards, or a concentrated outage event affecting multiple buildings.
evidence: 34 electrical complaints LAST WEEK vs. 15.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (123% increase)
Z-score of 3.77 indicates statistically significant spike
316 building permits filed in last 90 days (280 alterations) suggests active construction that may have damaged underground utilities
reporting_angles: Con Edison incident logs: were there outages or grid stress events in the district last week, particularly around major construction sites
Building safety angle: are older residential buildings (heat/hot water complaints rank #1 at 5,710) also experiencing electrical code violations

themes_detail.label: Lead Dust & Construction Safety
themes_detail.summary: Construction lead dust complaints spiked 700% TWO WEEKS AGO (3 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average)—a z-score of 5.42—coinciding with 316 building permit filings, indicating inadequate contractor compliance with lead-safe work practices in a district with vulnerable populations.
evidence: 3 construction lead dust complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 5.42)
316 building permit filings in last 90 days (280 alterations, 10 new buildings) indicates heavy active construction
Community Board requests funding for 'other public health issues,' suggesting unaddressed environmental hazards
reporting_angles: Department of Housing Preservation & Development enforcement: how many construction sites have been audited for lead-safe compliance; what penalties issued
Resident health impact: interview families in buildings undergoing renovation; test results from dust sampling near active sites

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Spread
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints quadrupled to 12 LAST WEEK versus a 3.0-per-week baseline—a 300% increase (z-score: 4.99)—indicating widespread trip hazards and ADA accessibility issues across the district that likely correlate with the concurrent street infrastructure crisis.
evidence: 12 sidewalk condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% increase)
Z-score of 4.99 indicates strong statistical signal
Coincides with street condition spike (37 complaints THIS WEEK), suggesting systemic infrastructure failure
reporting_angles: Mapping exercise: cross-reference all 49 complaints from both street and sidewalk spikes to identify geographic cluster; are certain blocks worst-hit (e.g., near 1727 Amsterdam ULURP site or construction zones)
Equity angle: interview seniors and disabled residents about accessibility barriers; which blocks are most dangerous

themes_detail.label: Elevator Outages Climbing
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints rose 94% to 15 LAST WEEK from a 7.8-per-week average—a z-score of 3.91—affecting high-rise residential buildings and posing mobility risks in a district with aging population segments requesting homebound elder services.
evidence: 15 elevator complaints LAST WEEK vs. 7.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (94% increase, z-score: 3.91)
Community Board budget request for 'outreach services to homebound older adults,' indicating known vulnerability of elderly residents
Elevator failures directly isolate seniors in high-rise buildings
reporting_angles: Building Department inspection data: which buildings have repeat elevator complaints; are maintenance violations cited
Resident stories: interview seniors trapped in apartments during elevator outages; how many days without service
